# help controliscsiport
controliscsiport - Control the characteristics of an iscsi port

SYNTAX
    The syntax for the controliscsiport command can be one of the following:
        controliscsiport addr <IP_address> <netmask|prefix_len> [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport allowpeer [-f] <false/true> <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport delete [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport discovery add [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <portal> <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport discovery remove [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <portal> <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport discovery rescan [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [<portal>] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport discovery show [<portal>] [<node:slot:port>]
        controliscsiport gw <gw_address> [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport iqn {show|update}
        controliscsiport mtu <mtusz_bytes> [-f] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport ping [<count>] <ipaddr> [-vlan <vlan_tag>] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport session login [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <portal> <iqn> <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport session logout [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <portal> <iqn> <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport session rescan [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [<portal> <iqn>] <node:slot:port>
        controliscsiport session show [<node:slot:port>]
        controliscsiport stgt  <sendtgt_grp> [-vlan <vlan_tag>] [-f] <node:slot:port>

SUBCOMMANDS
    allowpeer
        Allows the iSCSI port to be used for iSCSI initiator.
    addr
        Sets the IPv4 address and netmask, or IPv6 address and prefix length
        of the iSCSI port.
    discovery
        add
            Adds an iSCSI discovery portal for use by the iSCSI initiator.
        remove
            Removes an iSCSI discovery portal and discovered targets.
        rescan
            Perform a SendTargets discovery with the iSCSI initiator.
        show
            Shows iSCSI targets discovered by the iSCSI initiator
    gw
        Sets the gateway address of the iSCSI port.
    iqn
        show
            Displays the target iqn.
        update
            Updates the target iqn to the standard format.
    mtu
        Sets the maximum transmission unit (MTU) size for the iSCSI port.
    delete
        Deletes the iSCSI port configuration.
    ping
        Pings the specified IP address a specified number of times from the
        iSCSI port.
    session
        login
            Login to an iSCSI target with the iSCSI initiator.
        logout
            Logout of an iSCSI target with the iSCSI initiator.
        rescan
            Rescans active iSCSI initiator session(s).
        show
            Shows active iSCSI initiator session(s).
    stgt
        Sets the SendTargets Group Tag (STGT) for the iSCSI port.

DESCRIPTION
    The controliscsiport command is used to set properties of an iSCSI port.

AUTHORITY
    Super, Service
    Any role granted the port_control right

OPTIONS
    -f
        Do not ask for confirmation. The default is to ask for confirmation.

SPECIFIERS
    <IP_address>
        Indicates the IP address of the iSCSI target.

    <netmask>
        Indicates the IP netmask of the IPv4 iSCSI target.

    <prefix_len>
        Indicates the IP prefix length of the IPv6 iSCSI target.

    <gw_address>
        Indicates the IP address of the gateway.

    <mtusz_bytes>
        Indicates the MTU size in bytes.

    <count>
        Indicates the number of ping packets to send. If a value is specified,
        it should be an integer from 1 through 64. If a value is not specified,
        the default is one packet.

    <sendtgt_grp>
        Indicates the STGT of the iSCSI target.
        <sendtgt_grp> is an integer in the range [0-65535].

    <vlan_tag>
        Indicates the VLAN tag number (1 to 4094).

    <portal>
        Indicates the IP:port of the iSCSI target.
        The IP address is an IPv4 address.
        The port is an integer in the range [0-65535].

    <iqn>
        Indicates the iSCSI IQN of the iSCSI target.

    <node:slot:port>
        The physical location of the iSCSI target port.

NOTES
    Access to all domains is required to run this command.

EXAMPLES
    In the following example, iSCSI port configuration is deleted:

        cli% controliscsiport delete -f 1:1:1

    In the following example, iSCSI port 0:4:1 is given permission to act as an iSCSI initiator:

        cli% controliscsiport allowpeer true -f 0:4:1

    In the following example, a new portal for iSCSI initiator discovery is added on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport discovery add -f 172.19.0.2:3260 0:4:1

    In the following example, an iSCSI initiator SendTargets discovery for portal 172.19.0.2:3260 is performed on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport discovery rescan 172.19.0.2:3260 0:4:1

    In the following example, a portal for iSCSI initiator discovery is removed on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport discovery remove -f 172.19.0.2:3260 0:4:1

    In the following example, the targets discovered by the iSCSI initiator are shown:

        cli% controliscsiport discovery show

    In the following example, a previously discovered iSCSI target is logged into on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport session login -f 172.19.0.3:3260 iqn.2007-11.com.example:iqn 0:4:1

    In the following example, an active iSCSI initiator session is logged out of on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport session logout -f 172.19.0.3:3260 iqn.2007-11.com.example:iqn 0:4:1

    In the following example, an active iSCSI initiator session is rescanned on port 0:4:1:

        cli% controliscsiport session rescan 172.19.0.3:3260 iqn.2007-11.com.example:iqn 0:4:1

    In the following examples, the active iSCSI initiator sessions are shown:

        cli% controliscsiport session show
